This is a private UAB competition. The best-ranked teams on the final Codabench leaderboard earn up to +1 point on their final grade of the course. Participation is voluntary and does not affect the regular course assessment.

Final ranking distribution of extra points:
1st place
+1.0
2nd place
+0.75
3rd place
+0.5

• Every member of a team receives the same points.
• Ties in F1-score are broken by Sensitivity (recall), then by ROC AUC.

2. Data
The hidden patients and their patches come from clinical data of the Quiron dataset. They must not be downloaded, shared or reconstructed in any way. Any attempt to access them disqualifies the team.

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# Helicobacter Diagnosis Challenge

**This is a private UAB competition. Non UAB participants will not be accepted. **
Welcome! Your goal is to build a **MIL system for the diagnosis of *Helicobacter pylori*** from the analysis of WSI: given a set of patches (.png) cropped from a patient (e.g. `B22-25_0`), your model must return the **patient diagnosis** (e.g. **1** for positive cases with *Helicobacter*; **0** for negative ones without presence of the bacteria).

## How it works

- You train your model on your own computer using the **public training data** provided by the course.
- You submit your **code and trained weights**. The platform runs your model on a **hidden test set** that you never see, and gives you a score.
- The best scores appear on the **leaderboard**.

In the hidden sets the patient folders have **anonymous names** (`P001`, `P002`, …): you only get the patches.

## Calendar

| Phase | Dates | Data | Submissions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Development** | 10/11/2026 – 18/11/2026 (08:59) | Hidden development set | 5 per day |
| **Final** | 18/11/2026 (09:00) – 20/11/2026 (09:00) | Hidden final test set | 1 in total |

- **Development**: use this phase to check that your submission works and to compare ideas. Compare the baseline model with an ABMIL.
- **Final**: this is the one that counts. The final ranking is based on your **last** submission.

## Rules

- Work in teams of your class group.
- You have to use an **ABMIL** method.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

Each patient has a ground-truth diagnosis: **1** = positive (*H. pylori* present), **0** = negative.
Your model returns a **score in [0, 1]** for every patient.

## Decision

**score ≥ 0.5 → positive (1)**, **score < 0.5 → negative (0)**

## Ranking metric: F1-score

F1-score of the **positive class**, computed over **patients** (not patches):

- **Precision** = TP / (TP + FP) — of the patients you diagnosed as positive, how many really are
- **Recall** = TP / (TP + FN) — of the positive patients, how many you found
- **F1 = 2 · Precision · Recall / (Precision + Recall)**

### Development phase: F1 mean ± std over 10 random samples

To show how stable your result is, in the **Development** phase the F1 is computed on **10 random samples** of the hidden development patients. Each sample contains **80% of the patients**, drawn keeping the proportion of positive and negative cases. The samples are **the same for every team** (fixed random seeds), so scores are directly comparable.

The **F1** column of the leaderboard is the **mean of the 10 F1 values**. **This is the ranking column.**

The **standard deviation** of the 10 values, each individual value and the **F1 on all the patients** of the development set are shown in the **detailed results** of every submission (open them from the leaderboard row or from *My Submissions*): **F1 = mean ± std**.

Your model is run **only once**: the 10 samples are drawn from the same predictions, so this costs you nothing in time.

### Final phase

In the **Final** phase the **F1** column is the **F1 on all the patients** of the hidden final test set.

## Tie-break: Sensitivity

If two teams have the same F1 (4 decimals), the **Sensitivity** decides (higher is better):

**Sensitivity = Recall = TP / (TP + FN)** — the fraction of positive patients your model detects. In a screening context, missing a positive patient (FN) is the most costly error.

If they are still tied, the **ROC AUC** and then the **Precision** decide, and finally the earliest submission.

## Other columns

- **Sensitivity** is always shown in the leaderboard (it is the tie-break).
- **ROC AUC** is computed on your **raw scores** (no threshold), so returning only 0/1 gives a poor AUC.
- **Precision** is shown for feedback.

## Errors

- If your model **crashes on a patient**, or returns something that is not a number, that patient gets score 0 (negative). The rest are still evaluated.
- Scores outside [0, 1] are clipped to [0, 1].
- If your submission **crashes completely** or exceeds the **time limit**, it fails and gets no score.

pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
# How to submit

You submit a **.zip file** containing your code and your trained weights. The platform loads your model and runs it on the hidden patients.

## 1. Zip structure

The files must be at the **root** of the zip (not inside a folder):

```
my_submission.zip
├── model.py        ← required
└── weights/        ← your trained model files (any format)
```

You can add other `.py` files if `model.py` imports them.

## 2. The `Model` interface

`model.py` must define a class called `Model` with exactly this interface:

```python
class Model:
    def __init__(self, weights_dir: str):
        # Load your model here (feature extractor + ABMIL).
        # weights_dir is the path to your "weights/" folder.
        ...

    def predict(self, patch_paths: list) -> float:
        # patch_paths: list with the paths of ALL the .png patches of ONE patient
        # Return the PROBABILITY (0..1) that the patient is positive, e.g. 0.87
        ...
```

- `predict` is called **once per patient**, with the whole bag of patches of that patient.
- Patches are **PNG** images like the ones in the course dataset. Patients have **hundreds of patches** (the number varies a lot from patient to patient).
- **Not all the patches have the same size**: most are 256×256, but some are not. **Resize (or pad) every patch to a fixed size before stacking them into a batch**: `np.stack` / `torch.stack` crash with mixed sizes, and a crash makes that patient count as negative. The template in the starting kit (`load_patch`) already does it.
- In the hidden sets the patient folders have **anonymous names** (`P001`, `P002`, …) and the patches are named `00001.png`, `00002.png`, …
- Always return a **float**. If you are unsure, return your best guess, not an error.
- Scores ≥ 0.5 count as a positive diagnosis (see the **Evaluation** page).

## 3. Environment

Your code runs in a fixed environment. You **cannot install extra packages**.

- Python 3.11
- `torch`, `torchvision` (CPU only)
- `opencv-python-headless`, `numpy`, `pillow`
- `scikit-learn`, `scikit-image`

Important limits:

- **No GPU**: run your model on CPU (`device="cpu"`). Use `torch.no_grad()` and batch the patches of a patient through your feature extractor.
- **No internet**: all weights must be inside your zip. Do not download anything at runtime (e.g. no `pretrained=True`: save the pretrained weights in `weights/`).
- **Time limit**: **3 hours** in Development and **4 hours** in Final for the whole hidden set (Development: 58 patients, ~38,000 patches; Final: 58 patients, ~50,000 patches; between ~130 and ~7,400 patches per patient). As a reference, a ResNet18 encoder + ABMIL takes ~50 ms per patch on the platform CPU (~30 min for the Development set). Aim for **< 200 ms per patch** on a laptop CPU, including reading the images.
- **Memory**: some patients have more than 7,000 patches. Do not load all the images of a patient into one tensor: read and encode them **in batches** (e.g. 64 patches) and keep only the features.
- Keep your zip **under 600 MB** (code + weights). Smaller zips upload and start faster.

## 4. Test locally first!

You **will not see the logs** of your Final submission, so if something fails you won't know why. Always test with the provided `run_local.py` script (in the **starting kit**) before submitting.

Put some patients you did **not** train on in a folder, one sub-folder per patient:

```
my_val/
├── B22-25_0/      ← .png patches of this patient
├── B22-31_0/
├── ...
└── labels.csv     ← optional: ground truth (patient,label)
```

`labels.csv` (optional) must have a header and one row per patient, with `1` = positive and `0` = negative:

```
patient,label
B22-25_0,1
B22-31_0,0
```

### Run it

```bash
python run_local.py --submission my_submission.zip --data my_val/
```

It checks your zip structure, loads your model exactly like the platform does, and prints the F1 (mean ± std over 10 samples and on all patients), ROC AUC, precision, recall and the time per patient.

The starting kit also contains `example_submission/`, a minimal submission template that runs (it returns 0.5 for every patient: replace it with your model).

## 5. Submit

1. Go to the **My Submissions** tab.
2. Select the phase (**Development** or **Final**).
3. Upload your `.zip`.
4. Wait and check your score on the **Results** tab.
